transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-20 16:00 PDT | Duration: ~55 mins | Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya Thompson (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Jared Mills (Neptune - Dir ML), Sophia Li (Neptune SRE), Alyssa Grant (Neptune PM)
Shared artifacts: Runbook deck (link: https://redwood.app/poc/neptune/runbook), benchmark sheet (link: https://redwood.app/poc/neptune/benchmarks), security appendix (will be shared).

Summary: quick status check on onboarding milestone, creds handoff, staging env greenlight, and one outstanding perf anomaly around KV cache misses. Agreed next steps to run a dedicated benchmark and finalize VPC peering.

Top topics: onboarding progress, credentials (SSO/KMS), staging VPC peering, kv cache behavior, p50/p95 latency numbers, fallback strategy, security docs

00:00:05 Maya: okay good afternoon everyone, thanks for carving time. we'll do a quick milestone check, creds, then a short perf readout.
00:00:22 Jared: thanks Maya, we are on week three of the pilot, want to hit the greenlight for staging by friday so engineering can start smoke testing.
00:00:35 Priya: great, quick note — we saw the gateway auth token rotation issue in dev, was thinking that's probably the creds TTL mismatch.
00:00:47 Sophia: yeah we tried the automated token renewal, it sometimes fails when our k-m-s rotation is in flight, it looks like a time-skew thing.
00:01:10 Maya: ok that matches what Priya saw, we'll add an advisory for token TTL and Priya will run a repro.
00:01:28 Alyssa: also to be clear acceptance criteria: we need <100ms p50 and p95 <450ms for 512-token median prompts on staging, and kv cache hit rate > 80%.
00:01:50 Maya: noted. last run we were about 85ms p50 but p95 spiked to 620ms on one burst; priya, can you summarise the root cause?
00:02:05 Priya: sure, so the p95 spike correlated with a KV cache thrash — so what happened is prefix caching wasn't warming for those sessions, probably because sessions were routed to a different pod after autoscale. autoscale policy was set to aggressive and the warmup window small.
00:02:30 Jared: you mean K-V as in key value cache? sometimes transcripts show K-V cash (laughs)
00:02:38 Priya: yes kv cache, sorry, kv cache. and the other factor, and maybe this is my notation, our model variant had a slightly different quant profile so kernel selection changed and that added a few ms but the spike comes from cold kv.
00:02:55 Maya: got it. mitigation options?
00:03:02 Priya: we can do two things: increase warmup window and pin sessions for the pilot to avoid cross-pod routing, or use sticky routing by session-id. both are quick config changes.
00:03:20 Sophia: sticky routing is fine for staging, but will it affect throughput?
00:03:28 Priya: minimal effect for the scale you're planning, the bigger risk is capacity headroom. we can increase burst buffer to avoid cold starts.
00:03:40 Jared: what's the cost delta on burst buffer?
00:03:45 Maya: roughly estimated +10% for the dedicated pool while the pilot is active, we can give a more precise number after Priya's benchmark.
00:03:55 Priya: i'll run a 2-hour run at realistic traffic (we talked about ~60rps) and capture p50/p95 and token cost.
00:04:05 Alyssa: perfect. on the security side — we're waiting on the SOC 2 doc you mentioned and also need SSO metadata for SAML integration.
00:04:16 Maya: i'll send the SOC 2 appendix today, and priya will follow up with the SAML metadata format.
00:04:24 Sophia: also KMS; we want to validate envelope encryption with our HSM. how does Redwood handle KMS integration for private deployments?
00:04:37 Priya: for Redwood Private we support customer KMS via standard envelope encryption; we can integrate AWS KMS or a bring-your-own HSM through our connector. for hosted, we do BYOK with an approved transit path. there may be some handshake steps for cert exchange.
00:04:58 Jared: so for the pilot we will do a staging VPC peering + BYOK to keep keys in our account, correct?
00:05:07 Maya: that's the plan yes, and we'll run a call with your security team next week to complete cert exchange.
00:05:16 Priya: quick note on routing — we propose initial routing policy to prefer redwood-dedicated nodes in us-west then fallback to hosted if needed; fallback settings are in the runbook.
00:05:30 Alyssa: can you add the fallback section to the runbook? we want to review regression impacts.
00:05:36 Maya: will do. I'll add a short appendix on fallback behavior and example rollbacks.
00:05:44 Priya: okay next up — bench numbers from last night: p50 92ms avg for 512 tokens, p95 600ms during a controlled burst, token cost roughly 0.14 cents per token on current quant profile, kv hit rate averaged 74%.
00:06:05 Jared: 74% is below our 80% goal — what are the levers?
00:06:12 Priya: levers are prefix cache size, session pinning, and prompt canonicalization to increase reuse. we can also recommend a small policy tweak to prewarm top N keys.
00:06:26 Sophia: prompt canonicalization would need product alignment; Alyssa will own that.
00:06:32 Alyssa: yep i can do a small mapping to canonical templates for the first pass.
00:06:40 Maya: excellent.
00:06:50 Jared: any blocker for us to greenlight staging?
00:06:55 Sophia: main blockers: VPC peering pending, SAML metadata needed, and kv tuning; once we get SOC2 and peering we'll do a short smoke test.
00:07:10 Maya: timeline?
00:07:12 Sophia: if peering is provisioned tomorrow and priya runs the benchmark friday morning we can greenlight friday afternoon.
00:07:20 Priya: i'll queue the benchmark jobs asap, need the peering CIDR and a test dataset (small set) from you.
00:07:29 Jared: i'll have the CIDR to you by EOD and can drop a trimmed dataset in S3 link.
00:07:36 Priya: perfect.
00:07:45 Maya: re: legal/procurement, any remaining items?
00:07:49 Jared: procurement is fine for pilot, legal had one ask about audit logging retention — can you confirm retention window?
00:07:58 Maya: default retention is 90 days for trial tiers, enterprise options available; i'll include retention options in the security appendix.
00:08:06 Jared: great.
00:08:20 Priya: one more technical item — there's a minor mismatch in quant profile naming between your build and the model we onboarded; suggest we pin the model variant for consistency during pilot to avoid kernel flapping.
00:08:36 Sophia: pinning is fine for pilot.
00:08:40 Maya: ok we'll pin to redwood-chi-7b-q4 and note it in the runbook.
00:08:48 Alyssa: can you add a short how-to for rollback in the runbook in case we see quality regressions?
00:08:55 Priya: yes, i'll draft an A/B rollback recipe.
00:09:05 Maya: good. open questions from Neptune?
00:09:10 Jared: i think we covered it, quick ask — can we get a cost estimate for two scenarios: sticky routing + burst buffer vs no sticky routing and larger pool?
00:09:22 Maya: yes i'll get finance to give an estimate, priya will provide the perf numbers to feed that.
00:09:30 Priya: action: i'll run 3 permutations — sticky+burst, sticky only, and larger pool — and capture cost/token.
00:09:40 Sophia: rough timeframe for that?
00:09:43 Priya: 48 hours after peering completes.
00:09:46 Maya: anyone else?
00:09:50 Alyssa: no.
00:09:52 Maya: recap: Maya send SOC2 appendix & fallback appendix; Priya run benchmark and permutations; Sophia provision VPC peering and provide CIDR; Alyssa share acceptance criteria doc; Jared provide dataset link. We'll reconvene after Priya uploads benchmark.
00:10:12 Jared: thanks all.
00:10:18 [meeting continues — short technical side-discussion between Priya and Sophia about TLS cipher suites and cert pinning; audio overlaps and notes are brief]
00:15:40 Priya: TLS note — for peering we recommend cipher list x, and mutual TLS for the gateway; Sophia: ack will confirm with infra.
00:18:12 Maya: end of formal agenda, drop any follow-ups in the runbook comments, i'll ping via email.
00:18:25 [crosstalk, small scheduling details]
00:25:00 Priya: quick blow-by-blow of the benchmark plan: warmup 30m, 1h steady run at 60rps, 30m spike test at 120rps, collect p50/p95, kv hit rate, token cost. will upload sheet to link in runbook.
00:30:00 Sophia: noted.
00:40:00 Maya: thanks everyone, we'll aim for greenlight by friday.
00:40:10 Jared: thanks, appreciate it.
00:40:22 Meeting end: 16:55 PDT

Notes on transcription: occasional word swaps (k-v as K-V cash), product names slightly mis-heard (redwood-chi vs redwood-7b), punctuation and sentence breaks reflect spoken cadence rather than prose.
